title: O Lord, Our Heavenly King
description: O Lord, Our Heavenly King in Tonic Solfa to ST. BRIDE, doh is Bb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 8 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 8, part 1, headed “God's sovereignty and goodness; and man's dominion over the creatures”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. BRIDE; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O Lord, our heav-enly King, Thy name is all di-vine; Thy glo-ries round the earth are spread, And o'er the heavens they shine.

lines: Thy glories round the earth are spread,
And o'er the heavens they shine.
When to thy works on high
And see the moon complete in light
Lord, what is man, that worthless thing,
That thou shouldst love him so?
Next to thine angels he is plac'd,
And birds that cut the air with wings,
And fish that cleave the sea.
Of dust and worms thy power can frame
Out of the mouths of babes
And strike the world with awe.
Thy glories round the earth are spread,
And o'er the heavens they shine.

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. BRIDE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
